# omx-clap-core / fuzz_state

omx-clap-core's own fuzz target `fuzz_state` ([source](source/fuzz_state.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-clap-core 0.20.1 (FreeMixer/omx-clap-core at 246923f0).

Takes the input up to its first NUL, of at most 3 MiB, as the base64 text of a preset's state body and decodes it with preset_base64_decode, checking the answer against the harness's own reading of RFC 4648 base64 (whitespace skipped, padding optional). A decoded body is encoded again with preset_base64_encode, compared with the harness's own encoding, decoded back, and carried as state.bytes through a whole preset document written and read again. The text is then decoded, and the body encoded, with the allocation failing.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libomx-clap-readers.a of src/preset_file.c and src/lv2_locate.c of omx-clap-core 0.20.1 at commit 246923f0, and fuzz/alloc.c, compiled with each build's flags, as omx-clap-core's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- As in omx-clap-core's own fuzz build, the readers are compiled with fuzz/alloc.h forced on them, so their malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup and free go to fuzz/alloc.c, which counts the bytes the reader holds and can make one chosen allocation fail; the harness's own allocations use the C library directly.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The text decoded from three copies with different bytes after its NUL gets the same answer each time, and the same bytes whenever two of them decode: the decoder reads nothing past the NUL ([lines 133-155](source/fuzz_state.c#L133-L155)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- For a text of n characters the decoder holds at most n / 4 * 3 + 3 bytes ([lines 157-163](source/fuzz_state.c#L157-L163)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The decoder refuses exactly the texts the harness's own reading of RFC 4648 base64 refuses, and decodes every other text to the bytes the harness reads from it ([lines 165-186](source/fuzz_state.c#L165-L186)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A refused text returns no body, leaves the length it was handed unwritten, and gives back every byte the decoder allocated ([lines 188-202](source/fuzz_state.c#L188-L202)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Any text decoded with its allocation failing is refused cleanly in the same way, and a body encoded with the encoder's allocation failing returns no text and holds no memory ([lines 206-226](source/fuzz_state.c#L206-L226)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A decoded body encodes to the padded RFC 4648 text of (len + 2) / 3 * 4 characters, letter for letter the harness's own encoding, equal to the input when the input (without whitespace) is already that encoding, and decodes back to the same bytes ([lines 278-314](source/fuzz_state.c#L278-L314)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The encoded body set as state.bytes of a preset document, written and read back, decodes to the same bytes ([lines 229-264](source/fuzz_state.c#L229-L264)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch omx-clap-core` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
